chapters.title: Why HPR Sounds Monotone: Solo vs. Conversational Formats

quotes.text: As it turned out, monotone is a slippery word, as it can refer to both the sound of someone's speech, as well as a range of expression, both in sentiment and semantics.
A person reading from notes naturally has a flat pitch pattern than two or more people having a live conversation.
What is talked about is not just narrowing minded or stuck on one topic, if anything, the reverse is true.

In the code I used for this analysis was Librosa for basic audio analysis, then Parcel Math, Phonetics and WebRTC, VOD for voice detection, ScienceKit Learn or SK Learn for Pattern Detection, Spacy for Understanding Natural Language.

notes.summary: Lee investigates whether Hacker Public Radio episodes are 'monotone' by analyzing pitch variation and semantic content using Python tools. He compares HPR to other podcasts and TED Talks, finding that while speech pitch is flatter due to solo recordings, the range of topics is broad. The episode covers audio processing, sentiment analysis, and open-source libraries like Librosa and SciKit-learn.
